title: Help with high end graphics for my android game
author: Hjemmelegen
selftext:
I'm building a exploration open world game for android. Struggling to get the art/graphics good. Previously made a pretty cool and fairly good looking racing game, but this open world with multiple different worlds are obviously something else. 

Using Godot and Blender so far. Should I try Unreal engine instead? Or is there some other trick I'm missing? As you see from the attached image, its just not usable at this point. Anyone care to give me some pointers, guide or something to improve the graphics?

comments.author: redditscraperbot2
comments.body: Android is an android so for open world exploration stuff art direction should probably be carrying your game rather than graphics. Lighting and stuff can be baked to give the impression of depth and shadow without the hardware cost as well

comments.author: EffectNo2152
comments.body: hey im basically at the same spot as you right now. i think materials and lighting is the trick

replies.author: SeasawPhilosopher
replies.body: Yes, I just hit this and material and lighting make a huge difference. I just installed Substance Designer and Substance Painter, and Claude is using them to make much better textures and add layers to models for wear, dirt, rust, etc. It's way better than what I was getting from Blender and texture packs alone. Giving Claude the right tools for the job is proving to be what I needed.

replies.author: maddix_cummings
replies.body: I'm pretty sure Claude cannot paint layers on Substance Painter (API limits), only use procedural fills with masks, as you said for grunge maps, filters and more. Do you have an alternative workflow? Cause layering grunge maps is really easy and I have failed to see any upside in Claude against doing it myself.

replies.author: SeasawPhilosopher
replies.body:
I'm not entirely sure how it's implemented, because I've never used Painter myself, but I had Claude wire up a system where it tags models in blender with age and exposure (oil, rain, salt, etc.), and then it applies appropriate wear in painter. I'm sure an artist could do better but this allows me to work solo on larger levels. It's an evolving system, so we'll see how well it works, but so far I like the results.  


Claude did say this, which may explain how we get around the limit your describing.   
  
**Hand-painted detail doesn’t need the brush.** A script can import any image as a resource and use it as a fill’s source or as a mask. So a “painted” mask can be made somewhere else and brought in, for example one computed from the level in Blender.

replies.author: maddix_cummings
replies.body:
Well then it's not painting. And the response from Claude is a bit stupid, that's a very convoluted way of... using a brush. Because she is using the mask as an alpha cutout, which is how brushes work. It's also talking about "painted" masks, which is misrepresenting the actual Substance Painter workflow (fill and then mask, nothing to do with its workflow). 

Regardless, as a 3D artist I have a hard time seeing how there's any time gain in applying basic generators as Claude is doing. Also I believe in a lot with AI but I doubt it'll be painting layers in the next year, maybe aided with a curvature map and all... We can only wish.

replies.author: SeasawPhilosopher
replies.body: Appreciate the feedback. I don’t know man my expertise is in coding as I was software a engineer for 30 years and I think I’m pretty decent at game design and have been rapidly teaching myself all the other aspects of game dev to a sufficient level where I can work as creative director. It’s probably not done how an artist would but the results seemed good to me and it alows me to work on the 20 other things that need doing. But very likely I’ll learn more and rebuild that part of the system in a few months as has been happening with all my other game systems.

replies.author: EffectNo2152
replies.body:
Sweet. Look into texture ripper if you havent yet.

Is that map from real world data? if so you can probably find Sonar Bathymetry data get realworld depth and current flows of the water bodies

comments.author: Ball_Analytics
comments.body: reduce the draw distance, imo don't go all silent hill but work with the device you're aiming for.
